t:
Notwithstanding subsection (b) of section 14222 of Public Law 110–246 (7 U.S.C. 612c–6; in this section referred to as “section 14222”), none of the funds appropriated or otherwise made available by this or any other Act shall be used to pay the salaries and expenses of personnel to carry out a program under section 32 of the Act of August 24, 1935 (7 U.S.C. 612c; in this section referred to as “section 32”) in excess of $886,000,000 
(exclusive of carryover appropriations from prior fiscal years), as follows: Child Nutrition Programs Entitlement Commodities—$465,000,000; State Option Contracts— $5,000,000; Removal of Defective Commodities—$2,500,000; Administration of Section 32 Commodity Purchases—$35,440,000:  Provided, That of the total funds made available in the matter preceding this proviso that remain unobligated on October 1, 2017, such unobligated balances shall carryover into the next fiscal year and shall remain available until expended for any of the three stated purposes of section 32, except that any such carryover funds used in accordance with clause (3) of section 32 may not exceed $75,000,000 and may not be obligated until the Secretary of Agriculture provides written notification of the expenditures to the Committees on Appropriations of both Houses of Congress at least two weeks in advance:  Provided further, That none of the funds made available in this Act or any other Act shall be used for salaries and expenses to carry out in this fiscal year sub-section (i)(1)(E) of section 19 of the Richard B. Russell National School Lunch Act (42 U.S.C. 1769a), except in an amount that excludes the transfer of $125,000,000 of the funds to be transferred under subsection (c) of section 14222, until October 1, 2017:  Provided further, That $125,000,000 made available on October 1, 2017, to carry out such section 19 shall be excluded from the limitation described in subsection (b)(2)(A)(x) of section 14222:  Provided further, That, with the exception of any available carryover funds authorized in the first proviso of this section to be used for the purposes of clause (3) of section 32, none of the funds appropriated or otherwise made available by this or any other Act shall be used to pay the salaries or expenses of any employee of the Department of Agriculture or officer of the Commodity Credit Corporation to carry out clause (3) of section 32, or for any surplus removal activities or price support activities under section 5 of the Commodity Credit Corporation Charter Act (15 U.S.C. 714c):  Provided further, That the available unobligated balances under (b)(2)(A)(ix) of section 14222 in excess of the limitation set forth in this section, excluding the carryover amounts authorized in the first proviso of this section for section 32 and the amounts to be transferred pursuant to the second proviso of this section, are hereby permanently rescinded.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the advance written notification requirement is a participatory procedure, but the notification goes to the congressional Appropriations Committees, which are inside the federal government. The rest of the section is an appropriations limitation and rescission governing Section 32 funds. The mention of "State Option Contracts" is only a funding line item, not consultation with states, and no outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue.
fable.s: may not be obligated until the Secretary of Agriculture provides written notification of the expenditures to the Committees on Appropriations of both Houses of Congress at least two weeks in advance

opus.w: This section sets spending limits, carryover rules and rescissions for Section 32 funds. The only procedural step is advance notice to the congressional Appropriations Committees, and Congress is inside the federal government, so that step does not count as participation. No state, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, given a hearing or given a right to object or sue, and 'State Option Contracts' appears only as a funding line item.
opus.s: may not be obligated until the Secretary of Agriculture provides written notification of the expenditures to the Committees on Appropriations of both Houses of Congress at least two weeks in advance
opus.b: The tempting reading is to call this participation because the Secretary must give the Committees on Appropriations written notice before spending carryover funds. That fails the definition, because Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. "State Option Contracts" is only a budget line item, and it sets up no consultation with the states.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of Agriculture to notify Congressional Committees before obligating certain funds. However, Congress and its committees are part of the federal government. The definition explicitly states that reports to or notifications of Congress are inside the federal government and do not constitute participation. There is no involvement of outside parties such as the public, states, or private entities in the decision-making process described.
qwen_chat.s: except that any such carryover funds used in accordance with clause (3) of section 32 may not exceed $75,000,000 and may not be obligated until the Secretary of Agriculture provides written notification of the expenditures to the Committees on Appropriations of both Houses of Congress at least two weeks in advance
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement for the Secretary to notify Congressional Committees constitutes participation because it involves communication with an external body before an action (obligating funds). However, Congress is explicitly defined as being INSIDE the federal government. Therefore, notifications or reports to Congress are intra-governmental communications and do not count as participation under the provided definition.
